title: The Day a Billing Dispute Window Runs From
content:
The day the client's window to dispute a Private Event & Banquet Services bill runs from is settled by whether the desk raised the bill in time.

The days the desk took to raise the bill are counted from the day the event was delivered, or, where no delivered entry stands for the booking, from the day the booking's event was to have been held, up to the day the bill was raised.

1. Where the bill was raised later after the event than the days the package prints for raising it, and a delivered entry stands for the booking, the window runs from the day the event was delivered, the client having had the substance of the bill at the event itself.
2. Where the bill was raised later than those days and no delivered entry stands for the booking, the window runs from the day the booking's event was to have been held.
3. Where the bill was raised within those days, the window runs from the day the bill was raised.

A bill raised on exactly the number of days the package prints was raised within those days and falls in the third case.

## The days each package prints for raising the bill

| Package | Final bill raised by, calendar days after the event |
| --- | --- |
| Meeting Room Refreshment Package | 3 |
| Boardroom Reception Package | 5 |
| Conference Day Delegate Package | 7 |
| Seated Banquet Package | 10 |
| Gala Reception Package | 14 |
| Multi-Day Conference Residency Package | 21 |

## Illustrations on hypothetical records

An event on the Gala Reception Package was delivered and the bill raised 19 days afterwards. 19 is later than the 14 the package prints, and a delivered entry stands, so the window runs from the day the event was delivered. Had the bill been raised 14 days afterwards, the window would run from the day the bill was raised. Where no delivered entry stands for the booking and the bill was raised 30 days after the day the event was to have been held, the window runs from that day the event was to have been held.
